objects.definition: typedef int                             rt_bool_t;      /**< boolean type */
objects.description: Boolean integral type used by RT-Thread for true/false values. Non-zero is true; zero is false. Use with RT_TRUE/RT_FALSE macros.

objects.definition: typedef int8_t                          rt_int8_t;      /**<  8bit integer type */
objects.description: Signed 8-bit integer type alias used across RT-Thread. Falls back to 'signed char' if libc types are unavailable.

objects.definition: typedef int16_t                         rt_int16_t;     /**< 16bit integer type */
objects.description: Signed 16-bit integer type alias. May map to 'signed short' when libc is not used.

objects.definition: typedef int32_t                         rt_int32_t;     /**< 32bit integer type */
objects.description: Signed 32-bit integer type alias. May map to 'signed int' when libc is not used.

objects.definition: typedef uint8_t                         rt_uint8_t;     /**<  8bit unsigned integer type */
objects.description: Unsigned 8-bit integer type alias. May map to 'unsigned char' when libc is not used.

objects.definition: typedef uint16_t                        rt_uint16_t;    /**< 16bit unsigned integer type */
objects.description: Unsigned 16-bit integer type alias. May map to 'unsigned short' when libc is not used.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t                        rt_uint32_t;    /**< 32bit unsigned integer type */
objects.description: Unsigned 32-bit integer type alias. May map to 'unsigned int' when libc is not used.

objects.definition:
#ifdef RT_USING_LIBC
typedef int64_t                         rt_int64_t;     /**< 64bit integer type */
#else
#ifdef ARCH_CPU_64BIT
typedef signed long                     rt_int64_t;     /**< 64bit integer type */
#else
typedef signed long long                rt_int64_t;     /**< 64bit integer type */
#endif /* ARCH_CPU_64BIT */
#endif /* RT_USING_LIBC */
objects.description: Signed 64-bit integer type alias. Maps to int64_t when libc is available, otherwise to 'long' on 64-bit arch or 'long long' on 32-bit arch.

objects.definition:
#ifdef RT_USING_LIBC
typedef uint64_t                        rt_uint64_t;    /**< 64bit unsigned integer type */
#else
#ifdef ARCH_CPU_64BIT
typedef unsigned long                   rt_uint64_t;    /**< 64bit unsigned integer type */
#else
typedef unsigned long long              rt_uint64_t;    /**< 64bit unsigned integer type */
#endif /* ARCH_CPU_64BIT */
#endif /* RT_USING_LIBC */
objects.description: Unsigned 64-bit integer type alias. Maps to uint64_t with libc, otherwise to 'unsigned long' on 64-bit arch or 'unsigned long long' on 32-bit arch.

objects.definition:
#ifdef ARCH_CPU_64BIT
typedef rt_int64_t                      rt_base_t;      /**< Nbit CPU related data type */
#else
typedef rt_int32_t                      rt_base_t;      /**< Nbit CPU related data type */
#endif
objects.description: Signed native word-size integer type for the target CPU (32-bit or 64-bit). Often used for return codes, counters, and signed handles.

objects.definition:
#ifdef ARCH_CPU_64BIT
typedef rt_uint64_t                     rt_ubase_t;     /**< Nbit unsigned CPU related data type */
#else
typedef rt_uint32_t                     rt_ubase_t;     /**< Nbit unsigned CPU related data type */
#endif
objects.description: Unsigned native word-size integer type for the target CPU. Used for sizes, bitmasks, and handles.

objects.definition:
#if defined(RT_USING_LIBC) && !defined(RT_USING_NANO)
typedef size_t                          rt_size_t;      /**< Type for size number */
#else
typedef rt_ubase_t                      rt_size_t;      /**< Type for size number */
#endif
objects.description: Unsigned size type used by RT-Thread APIs. Maps to C size_t when full libc is used, else to rt_ubase_t.

objects.definition:
#if defined(RT_USING_LIBC) && !defined(RT_USING_NANO)
typedef ssize_t                         rt_ssize_t;     /**< Used for a count of bytes or an error indication */
#else
typedef rt_base_t                       rt_ssize_t;     /**< Used for a count of bytes or an error indication */
#endif /* defined(RT_USING_LIBC) && !defined(RT_USING_NANO) */
objects.description: Signed size type for byte counts or error returns. Maps to POSIX ssize_t with libc, otherwise to rt_base_t.

objects.definition:
#if defined(RT_USING_LIBC) && !defined(RT_USING_NANO)
typedef intptr_t                        rt_intptr_t;    /**< Type for signed pointer length integer */
#else
typedef rt_base_t                      rt_intptr_t;    /**< Type for signed pointer length integer */
#endif /* defined(RT_USING_LIBC) && !defined(RT_USING_NANO) */
objects.description: Signed integer type capable of holding a pointer value. Maps to C intptr_t with libc, else rt_base_t.

objects.definition:
#if defined(RT_USING_LIBC) && !defined(RT_USING_NANO)
typedef uintptr_t                       rt_uintptr_t;   /**< Type for unsigned pointer length integer */
#else
typedef rt_ubase_t                       rt_uintptr_t;   /**< Type for unsigned pointer length integer */
#endif /* defined(RT_USING_LIBC) && !defined(RT_USING_NANO) */
objects.description: Unsigned integer type capable of holding a pointer value. Maps to C uintptr_t with libc, else rt_ubase_t.

objects.definition: typedef rt_base_t                       rt_err_t;       /**< Type for error number */
objects.description: Error code type used by RT-Thread APIs. Conventionally non-zero indicates error; exact codes defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: typedef rt_uint32_t                     rt_tick_t;      /**< Type for tick count */
objects.description: System tick count type (unsigned 32-bit). Used for timeouts and scheduling tick values.

objects.definition: typedef rt_base_t                       rt_flag_t;      /**< Type for flags */
objects.description: Flag bitfield type, signed native word-size. Used for option/flag sets in RT-Thread.

objects.definition: typedef rt_ubase_t                      rt_dev_t;       /**< Type for device */
objects.description: Device identifier/handle integer type (unsigned native word-size).

objects.definition: typedef rt_base_t                       rt_off_t;       /**< Type for offset */
objects.description: Offset type used in RT-Thread I/O. Signed native word-size.

Atomic integer type used for lock-free operations and refcounts. Implementation maps to C11 _Atomic(rt_base_t) when available, otherwise to plain rt_base_t or hardware-backed atomic type. Atomic semantics depend on platform/configuration.
Doubly-linked list node used by RT-Thread intrusive list utilities. Each embedded in containing objects for list membership.
Singly-linked list node for intrusive single lists.

Lockless singly-linked list node. Next pointer stored in an atomic integer to support concurrent operations without locks. Exact encoding of next pointer depends on rt_atomic_t width and casting in implementation (not shown here).

Spinlock primitive used for short critical sections. On SMP, wraps an architecture-specific rt_hw_spinlock_t; on non-SMP, implemented as a simple rt_ubase_t flag. Optional debug fields track owner and critical nesting. Initialize with RT_SPINLOCK_INIT or RT_DEFINE_SPINLOCK(name).

objects.definition: typedef rt_uint8_t rt_sched_thread_status_t;
objects.description: Alias for a thread scheduling status value stored as an 8-bit unsigned integer. Exact status semantics are not defined in this header and depend on the kernel’s status encoding.

Per-thread private scheduler state. Holds ticks and priority bookkeeping, including masks for priority mapping when RT_THREAD_PRIORITY_MAX > 32. Intended for internal use; callers should not access fields directly.

objects.definition:
struct rt_sched_thread_ctx
{
    rt_list_t                   thread_list_node;       /**< node in thread list */

    rt_uint8_t                  stat;                   /**< thread status */
    rt_uint8_t                  sched_flag_locked:1;    /**< calling thread have the scheduler locked */
    rt_uint8_t                  sched_flag_ttmr_set:1;  /**< thread timer is start */

#ifdef ARCH_USING_HW_THREAD_SELF
    rt_uint8_t                  critical_switch_flag:1; /**< critical switch pending */
#endif /* ARCH_USING_HW_THREAD_SELF */

#ifdef RT_USING_SMP
    rt_uint8_t                  bind_cpu;               /**< thread is bind to cpu */
    rt_uint8_t                  oncpu;                  /**< process on cpu */

    rt_base_t                   critical_lock_nest;     /**< critical lock count */
#endif

    struct rt_sched_thread_priv sched_thread_priv;      /**< private context of scheduler */
};
objects.description: Per-thread public scheduler context. Contains scheduling-visible state such as list linkage, status, flags, optional SMP CPU binding fields, and embeds the private scheduler state. Access requires holding the scheduler lock.

objects.definition: typedef rt_ubase_t rt_sched_lock_level_t;
objects.description: Scheduler lock level token type, used to save/restore lock state when calling rt_sched_lock/rt_sched_unlock.
Descriptor used (on MSVC and RT_DEBUGING_AUTO_INIT) to place init function metadata (level, function pointer, and name) into a special linker section for auto-initialization.
Descriptor used (on MSVC without RT_DEBUGING_AUTO_INIT) to place init function metadata (level and function) into a special section.
Descriptor used (non-MSVC with RT_DEBUGING_AUTO_INIT) to place init function name and pointer into a named section for auto-initialization.
Base kernel object header embedded in most RT-Thread kernel objects. Holds name, type, flags, and linkage into global object lists. Not constructed directly by an API here.

objects.definition: typedef rt_err_t (*rt_object_iter_t)(rt_object_t object, void *data);
objects.description: Iterator callback type used with rt_object_for_each-style iteration. Returns EOK to continue, positive to break success, negative errno to break on failure. The actual iterator API is not in this header.

objects.definition:

objects.description: Enumeration of kernel object classes used in object management and introspection.
Holds registration data for a kernel object class: its type, list head of instances, size, and a spinlock. Used internally by object management.

objects.definition: typedef void (*rt_timer_func_t)(void *parameter);
objects.description: Callback prototype for rt_timer timeout handlers.
Kernel software timer object supporting one-shot and periodic timing with skip-list scheduling. Embedded inside threads for time slicing/timeouts.
CPU usage accounting bucket counters (ticks) for user, system, IRQ, and idle time.
Per-CPU scheduler context and bookkeeping. Fields vary with SMP and config; tracks current/idle threads, ready queues, tick count, irq nesting, and optional stats.
Opaque interrupt context handle used to chain nested interrupt frames. Holds arch-specific context pointer and singly-linked list node.
Helper container for a wakeup callback and user data, used by SMART/LWP features to wake threads waiting on IPC.
User-space compatible signal action structure for LWP mode, similar to POSIX sigaction with mask, flags, and restorer.
Extension payload for specific signals in LWP mode (currently SIGCHLD fields).
Kernel-side signal information node used in LWP signal queues. Contains basic signal metadata and optional extension pointer.
Signal queue for an LWP thread: pending signal set and list of queued siginfo nodes.
Per-thread LWP signal state: mask and queue of pending signals.
User-space context snapshot embedded in thread when SMART/user mode is enabled. Holds user SP/PC/flags and arch-specific context pointer.

objects.definition: typedef void (*rt_thread_cleanup_t)(struct rt_thread *tid);
objects.description: Callback invoked when a thread exits for cleanup actions.
Thread Control Block containing scheduling state, stack info, timers, IPC relations, optional signal/LWP and debug fields, and per-thread data. Created via thread APIs (not present here).
Base header for IPC kernel objects, embedding rt_object and a list of suspended threads waiting on the IPC.
Counting semaphore IPC object with max and current value and a spinlock for protection.
Priority-inheritance/ceiling capable mutex IPC object with owner tracking and hold count.
Bitmask-based event object supporting AND/OR and clear operations; threads wait for bit conditions.
Fixed-size message mailbox delivering pointer-sized messages with a ring buffer and sender-wait queue.
Message queue object for fixed-size messages with internal free/used linked lists and sender suspension.
Generic heap-like memory manager descriptor tracking algorithm name, base address, and usage statistics. Aliased for smallmem/slab backends.
Block header used by the memheap allocator to link allocated and free blocks; contains magic for integrity checks.
Memheap allocator object managing a contiguous heap area with free/used lists and an internal semaphore for concurrency control.
Fixed-block memory pool (partition) with waiters list and spinlock; manages blocks via a simple list.
Virtual function table for device operations when RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS is enabled.
Wait queue used for POSIX-style polling and event notification on devices or channels.
Core RT-Thread device object representing a character/block/etc device with operation callbacks, class/type, flags, refcount, and optional DM/OFW integration.
Small helper to bind a notify callback to a device instance.
Kernel channel IPC for SMART/LWP: supports message wait queues, reply thread, pollable reader queue, status, and refcount.

Doubly linked list node type used by the list helpers in this header (rt_list_init/insert/remove/etc.). The concrete struct definition is not present in this header and is expected to come from rtdef.h.

Singly linked list node type used by the slist helpers in this header (rt_slist_init/append/insert/etc.). The concrete struct definition is not present in this header and is expected to come from rtdef.h. Macros and inline functions here manipulate its next pointer.
Enumeration of cache operation kinds used by CPU cache operation APIs (instruction/data cache ops). Values indicate flush or invalidate operations.

objects.definition: typedef void (*rt_isr_handler_t)(int vector, void *param);
objects.description: Typedef for an interrupt service routine function pointer. Handlers receive an interrupt vector number and a user parameter. Constructed by assigning a function with this signature. Destruction is not applicable.

Interrupt descriptor holding an ISR handler and its parameter; optionally tracks name and per-CPU counters when enabled via configuration macros. Instances are typically managed by the interrupt subsystem; this header does not provide an explicit constructor.
Single stack frame record for the hardware backtrace service, containing frame pointer (fp) and program counter (pc). Used with rt_hw_backtrace_frame_get/unwind.

Lock-less singly linked list node type used by the helper functions rt_ll_slist_init/enqueue/dequeue in this header. The node is expected to have an atomic-compatible next field (stored as rt_base_t) named next. The exact struct layout is not defined in this header and must be provided elsewhere (likely in rthw.h).

Atomic integer type used throughout this header for lock-free operations. Its exact underlying type is not defined here (it is defined elsewhere, likely in rthw.h). All atomic APIs in this header operate on pointers to this type.

Symbol table entry used when RT_USING_MODULE is enabled. Each entry holds an address for a symbol (function or variable) and its name. Primarily used to export symbols from a module so they can be resolved at runtime by the RT-Thread module system. The structure contains a generic pointer to the symbol and a const char pointer to its name string.

Node structure used internally by the message queue implementation to link queued messages. Each node holds the message length and, optionally, a priority when message-queue priority is enabled. Not intended for direct use by applications; managed by the RT-Thread MQ APIs.

functions.name: rt_sched_lock
functions.description: Acquire the system scheduler lock and return the previous lock level via plvl. Intended to prevent task scheduling while critical operations are performed. Use the returned level with rt_sched_unlock or rt_sched_unlock_n_resched to restore the prior state.
requirements: plvl must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable storage.
The returned lock level must be passed back to a matching rt_sched_unlock(...) or rt_sched_unlock_n_resched(...) call to correctly restore the prior scheduler state.
Lock/unlock calls should be balanced within the same execution context (e.g., same thread).
Error codes and exact semantics of the return value are unknown; callers must check and handle non-success results as per project conventions.

functions.name: rt_sched_unlock
functions.description: Release or restore the scheduler lock state using a previously saved lock level. Typically called after rt_sched_lock to re-enable scheduling without forcing an immediate reschedule.
requirements: level must be the exact value previously obtained from a successful rt_sched_lock call in the same execution context.
Lock/unlock operations must be balanced; do not unlock more times than locked.
May not perform an immediate reschedule; if rescheduling is needed, use rt_sched_unlock_n_resched.
Error codes and exact semantics of the return value are unknown; callers must check and handle non-success results as per project conventions.

functions.name: rt_sched_unlock_n_resched
functions.description: Release or restore the scheduler lock state using a previously saved lock level and, if appropriate, trigger a reschedule immediately after unlocking.
requirements: level must be the exact value previously obtained from a successful rt_sched_lock call in the same execution context.
Lock/unlock operations must be balanced; do not unlock more times than locked.
Calling context must allow rescheduling; specific constraints are unknown from this header.
Error codes and exact semantics of the return value are unknown; callers must check and handle non-success results as per project conventions.

functions.name: rt_sched_is_locked
functions.description: Query whether the scheduler is currently locked in the calling context. Useful for assertions or conditional behavior that depends on scheduling being disabled.
requirements: No arguments; callable whenever a Boolean indication of scheduler lock state is needed.
Exact meaning in interrupt or special contexts is unknown.

functions.name: rt_list_init
functions.description: Initialize a doubly-linked list head node so that it forms an empty list (next and prev point to itself). Typical usage: call once on a list head before inserting any nodes.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a rt_list_t object.
Call this before other list operations on this list head.
The memory backing l must be writable.

functions.name: rt_list_insert_after
functions.description: Insert node n immediately after node l in a doubly-linked circular list.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a node that is part of an initialized, well-formed list.
n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a node; its links will be overwritten.
The memory backing l and n must be writable.
Behavior assumes l->next and l->prev are valid (i.e., l is in a proper list).

functions.name: rt_list_insert_before
functions.description: Insert node n immediately before node l in a doubly-linked circular list.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a node that is part of an initialized, well-formed list.
n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a node; its links will be overwritten.
The memory backing l and n must be writable.
Behavior assumes l->next and l->prev are valid (i.e., l is in a proper list).

functions.name: rt_list_remove
functions.description: Remove node n from its current doubly-linked circular list and reinitialize n so that n->next and n->prev point to itself.
requirements: n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a node currently linked into a well-formed list (n->next and n->prev must be valid).
The memory backing the involved nodes must be writable.

functions.name: rt_list_isempty
functions.description: Return nonzero if the list referenced by head l is empty; zero otherwise. An empty list has l->next == l.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a list head that has been initialized.
The list must be well-formed (circular with head pointing to itself when empty).

functions.name: rt_list_len
functions.description: Compute and return the number of nodes in the list referenced by head l by traversing until the traversal returns to l.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized list head.
The list must be a well-formed circular list; otherwise the traversal may loop indefinitely or access invalid memory.

functions.name: rt_slist_init
functions.description: Initialize a singly-linked list head so that it represents an empty list (next set to RT_NULL).
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a rt_slist_t object.
Call this before other singly-linked list operations on this list head.
The memory backing l must be writable.

functions.name: rt_slist_append
functions.description: Append node n to the tail of the singly-linked list whose head is l. After appending, n->next is set to RT_NULL.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the list head or a node in the list; typically the head node initialized with rt_slist_init.
The list reachable from l must be properly terminated with a NULL next pointer to avoid infinite traversal.
n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer; n->next will be overwritten and set to RT_NULL (n should not be part of another list).
The memory backing all involved nodes must be writable.

functions.name: rt_slist_insert
functions.description: Insert node n immediately after head l (i.e., at the beginning of the singly-linked list).
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the list head (initialized).
n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer; n->next will be overwritten.
The memory backing l and n must be writable.

functions.name: rt_slist_len
functions.description: Return the number of nodes in the singly-linked list following head l by traversing until a NULL next pointer is encountered.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized list head.
The list must be properly NULL-terminated; otherwise traversal may access invalid memory or loop indefinitely.

functions.name: rt_slist_pop
functions.description: Remove and return the first node after head l in a singly-linked list. If the list is empty, returns RT_NULL. The removed node's next is set to RT_NULL.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the list head (initialized).
The list must be properly formed (either empty, or with a valid first node).
The memory backing l and the removed node must be writable.

functions.name: rt_slist_remove
functions.description: Search the singly-linked list starting at head l for node n and remove it if found. Returns l. If n is removed, n->next is set to RT_NULL.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the list head (initialized).
n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a node; if found, its next will be overwritten.
The list must be properly NULL-terminated to ensure traversal completes.
The memory backing the involved nodes must be writable.

functions.name: rt_slist_first
functions.description: Return the first node after head l in the singly-linked list (l->next). May return RT_NULL if the list is empty.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the list head (initialized).

functions.name: rt_slist_tail
functions.description: Return the last node in the singly-linked list reachable from l by traversing next pointers until RT_NULL. If the list is empty when l is a head node, returns l itself as no traversal occurs.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to the list head or a node within the list.
The list must be properly NULL-terminated; otherwise traversal may not terminate.

functions.name: rt_slist_next
functions.description: Return the next node after n in a singly-linked list (n->next). May return RT_NULL at the end of the list.
requirements: n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a node in a singly-linked list.

functions.name: rt_slist_isempty
functions.description: Return nonzero if the singly-linked list represented by head l is empty (l->next == RT_NULL); zero otherwise.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized list head.

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_icache_enable
functions.description: Enables the CPU instruction cache (I-Cache). Intended to be called early during platform initialization to improve instruction fetch performance. Note: when RT_USING_CACHE is not enabled at build time, this identifier is a no-op macro rather than a real function.
requirements: Available as a real function only when RT_USING_CACHE is defined; otherwise it expands to an empty macro
Must be called in a context where enabling the I-Cache is safe for the platform (exact timing/platform rules are unknown)

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_icache_disable
functions.description: Disables the CPU instruction cache (I-Cache). Useful for low-level operations that require coherent instruction fetch or during shutdown. Note: when RT_USING_CACHE is not enabled, this is a no-op macro.
requirements: Available as a real function only when RT_USING_CACHE is defined; otherwise it expands to an empty macro
Call only when it is safe to disable I-Cache on the target platform (exact rules unknown)

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_icache_status
functions.description: Returns the current status of the CPU instruction cache (I-Cache). The exact meaning of the return value is platform-defined (typically non-zero for enabled, zero for disabled). When RT_USING_CACHE is not enabled, this is a macro returning 0.
requirements: Available as a real function only when RT_USING_CACHE is defined; otherwise it expands to a macro returning 0
Caller should interpret the return code according to the platform port (exact values unknown)

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_icache_ops
functions.signature: void rt_hw_cpu_icache_ops(int ops, void* addr, int size);
functions.description: Performs I-Cache maintenance operations over a given memory range. The ops bitmask uses RT_HW_CACHE_OPS values (RT_HW_CACHE_FLUSH, RT_HW_CACHE_INVALIDATE). Intended for ensuring instruction coherency after code patching or loading. When RT_USING_CACHE is not enabled, this is a no-op macro.
requirements: Available as a real function only when RT_USING_CACHE is defined; otherwise it expands to an empty macro
ops should be a combination of RT_HW_CACHE_FLUSH and/or RT_HW_CACHE_INVALIDATE
addr must be a valid pointer to the start of the memory region
size must be non-negative and represent the number of bytes to operate on
The memory range [addr, addr+size) must be accessible and mapped for the CPU

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_dcache_enable
functions.description: Enables the CPU data cache (D-Cache). Typically used during system bring-up to improve data access performance. When RT_USING_CACHE is not enabled, this is a no-op macro.
requirements: Available as a real function only when RT_USING_CACHE is defined; otherwise it expands to an empty macro
Should be called only when enabling D-Cache is safe for the platform (exact rules unknown)

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_dcache_disable
functions.description: Disables the CPU data cache (D-Cache). Useful when cache coherency cannot be maintained or before shutdown. When RT_USING_CACHE is not enabled, this is a no-op macro.
requirements: Available as a real function only when RT_USING_CACHE is defined; otherwise it expands to an empty macro
Call only when it is safe to disable D-Cache on the target platform (exact rules unknown)

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_dcache_status
functions.description: Returns the current status of the CPU data cache (D-Cache). The exact meaning of the return value is platform-defined (commonly non-zero for enabled, zero for disabled). When RT_USING_CACHE is not enabled, this is a macro returning 0.
requirements: Available as a real function only when RT_USING_CACHE is defined; otherwise it expands to a macro returning 0
Caller should interpret the return code according to the platform port (exact values unknown)

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_dcache_ops
functions.signature: void rt_hw_cpu_dcache_ops(int ops, void* addr, int size);
functions.description: Performs D-Cache maintenance operations over a given memory range. The ops bitmask uses RT_HW_CACHE_OPS values (RT_HW_CACHE_FLUSH, RT_HW_CACHE_INVALIDATE). Use for data coherency with DMA or self-modifying code. When RT_USING_CACHE is not enabled, this is a no-op macro.
requirements: Available as a real function only when RT_USING_CACHE is defined; otherwise it expands to an empty macro
ops should be a combination of RT_HW_CACHE_FLUSH and/or RT_HW_CACHE_INVALIDATE
addr must be a valid pointer to the start of the memory region
size must be non-negative and represent the number of bytes to operate on
The memory range [addr, addr+size) must be accessible and mapped for the CPU

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_reset
functions.description: Performs a hardware reset of the CPU/platform. Intended for fatal error recovery or reboot routines.
requirements: Should be called in a context where an immediate system reset is acceptable (effects are platform-wide)
No return is typically expected; caller should not rely on any cleanup after this call

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_shutdown
functions.description: Shuts down the CPU/platform. Typically powers off or halts execution depending on the target port.
requirements: Should be called only when a system shutdown is intended
Post-call execution may not continue; caller should not expect to return

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_arch
functions.description: Returns a textual identifier for the CPU architecture/port in use (e.g., architecture name or port string). Useful for logging and diagnostics.
requirements: Returned pointer refers to static storage or platform-defined string; do not free
Exact string format is platform-specific

functions.name: rt_hw_stack_init
functions.description: Initializes a thread stack frame for a new thread, preparing it to start at entry(parameter) and to call exit on thread exit. Returns the new stack pointer to use when starting the thread.
requirements: entry must be a valid function pointer with prototype compatible with the thread entry used by the port (exact prototype unknown)
exit must be a valid function pointer to be invoked when the thread function returns (exact prototype unknown)
stack_addr must point to valid stack memory; conventional RT-Thread ports pass the stack top address (exact alignment/ordering unknown)
parameter is passed to the thread entry and may be NULL
Caller must use the returned pointer as the initial SP when creating the thread context

functions.name: rt_hw_stack_guard_init
functions.description: Initializes hardware stack guard/protection for a thread to detect stack overflows or violations. Available only when RT_USING_HW_STACK_GUARD is enabled.
requirements: Available only if RT_USING_HW_STACK_GUARD is defined at build time
thread must be a valid initialized rt_thread_t handle

functions.name: rt_hw_interrupt_init
functions.description: Initializes the hardware interrupt controller and RT-Thread interrupt handling framework. Should be called during early system initialization before enabling interrupts.
requirements: Must be called before installing/unmasking interrupts
Must be called in a context with interrupts disabled or appropriate for platform initialization (exact ordering unknown)

functions.name: rt_hw_interrupt_mask
functions.description: Masks/disables the specified interrupt vector so it will not trigger. Useful for temporarily disabling an IRQ.
requirements: vector must refer to a valid interrupt vector supported by the platform
Caller must ensure masking is appropriate for the system state to avoid lost critical interrupts

functions.name: rt_hw_interrupt_umask
functions.description: Unmasks/enables the specified interrupt vector so it can trigger. Used to allow handling of a given IRQ.
requirements: vector must refer to a valid interrupt vector supported by the platform
Interrupt must have been initialized/installed as needed before unmasking

functions.name: rt_hw_interrupt_install
functions.signature: rt_isr_handler_t rt_hw_interrupt_install(int vector, rt_isr_handler_t handler, void *param, const char *name);
functions.description: Installs or replaces the ISR for a given interrupt vector, associating a handler, its parameter, and an optional name (if interrupt info is enabled). Returns the previous handler.
requirements: vector must refer to a valid interrupt vector supported by the platform
handler may be NULL to uninstall/disable callback depending on port policy (exact behavior unknown)
param is passed to the handler when the interrupt fires and may be NULL
name may be NULL; used only if RT_USING_INTERRUPT_INFO is enabled
Caller should store the returned previous handler if it needs to restore it later

functions.name: rt_hw_interrupt_uninstall
functions.signature: void rt_hw_interrupt_uninstall(int vector, rt_isr_handler_t handler, void *param);
functions.description: Uninstalls a previously installed ISR for a given interrupt vector, matching on handler and param where applicable. Effectively clears or restores the vector to a default state depending on implementation.
requirements: vector must refer to a valid interrupt vector supported by the platform
handler should match the one previously installed for deterministic uninstall (exact matching policy unknown)
param should match the parameter used during installation (if required by implementation)

functions.name: rt_hw_local_irq_disable
functions.description: Disables local CPU interrupts and returns the previous interrupt level/state for later restoration. In SMP builds this is a real function; in non-SMP builds it aliases to rt_hw_interrupt_disable.
requirements: In SMP builds (RT_USING_SMP defined) this is available as a real function
In non-SMP builds this name is a macro alias to rt_hw_interrupt_disable
Caller must save the returned state and later pass it to rt_hw_local_irq_enable to restore

functions.name: rt_hw_local_irq_enable
functions.description: Restores local CPU interrupt state to a previously saved level. In SMP builds this is a real function; in non-SMP builds it aliases to rt_hw_interrupt_enable.
requirements: In SMP builds (RT_USING_SMP defined) this is available as a real function
In non-SMP builds this name is a macro alias to rt_hw_interrupt_enable
level must be a value previously returned by rt_hw_local_irq_disable or equivalent

functions.name: rt_cpus_lock
functions.description: Disables preemption and interrupts across all CPUs (global CPU lock) and returns a token/level to restore later. Available only in SMP builds.
requirements: Available only if RT_USING_SMP is defined; absent otherwise
Caller must later pass the returned level to rt_cpus_unlock to restore the previous state
Used to protect critical sections requiring global exclusion

functions.name: rt_cpus_unlock
functions.description: Restores the system state (preemption/interrupts) previously saved by rt_cpus_lock. Available only in SMP builds.
requirements: Available only if RT_USING_SMP is defined; absent otherwise
level must be the exact value returned by a matching rt_cpus_lock call
Must be called to avoid deadlock or permanently disabled interrupts

functions.name: rt_hw_interrupt_disable
functions.description: Disables interrupts and returns the previous interrupt state for later restoration. In SMP builds this is a macro alias to rt_cpus_lock; in non-SMP builds it is a real function.
requirements: In SMP builds (RT_USING_SMP defined) this name is a macro alias to rt_cpus_lock
In non-SMP builds this is available as a real function
Caller must save the returned state and later pass it to rt_hw_interrupt_enable to restore

functions.name: rt_hw_interrupt_enable
functions.description: Restores interrupt state to a previously saved level. In SMP builds this is a macro alias to rt_cpus_unlock; in non-SMP builds it is a real function.
requirements: In SMP builds (RT_USING_SMP defined) this name is a macro alias to rt_cpus_unlock
In non-SMP builds this is available as a real function
level must be a value previously returned by rt_hw_interrupt_disable or equivalent

functions.name: rt_hw_interrupt_is_disabled
functions.description: Returns whether interrupts are currently disabled. Useful for assertions or conditional behavior in critical sections.
requirements: Return semantics are platform-defined boolean (RT_TRUE/RT_FALSE)
Should be callable from any context; exact constraints are platform-specific

functions.name: rt_hw_context_switch
functions.signature: void rt_hw_context_switch(rt_ubase_t from, rt_ubase_t to, struct rt_thread *to_thread);
functions.description: Performs a context switch between two threads on SMP builds, switching from context 'from' to 'to' and informing the target thread pointer. Used by the scheduler.
requirements: Available in this signature only when RT_USING_SMP is defined
from and to are architecture-specific context stack pointers or context tokens
to_thread must be a valid pointer to the destination thread control block

functions.name: rt_hw_context_switch_to
functions.description: Starts execution by switching to a new thread context on SMP builds. Used when launching the first thread on a CPU.
requirements: Available in this signature only when RT_USING_SMP is defined
to is an architecture-specific initial context pointer/token
to_thread must be a valid pointer to the destination thread control block

functions.name: rt_hw_context_switch_interrupt
functions.signature: void rt_hw_context_switch_interrupt(void *context, rt_ubase_t from, rt_ubase_t to, struct rt_thread *to_thread);
functions.description: Performs a context switch from interrupt context on SMP builds. The 'context' carries interrupt frame data; switches from 'from' to 'to' and targets 'to_thread'.
requirements: Available in this signature only when RT_USING_SMP is defined
context must point to a valid interrupt/trap frame (exact structure unknown)
from and to are architecture-specific context pointers/tokens
to_thread must be a valid pointer to the destination thread control block

functions.name: rt_hw_backtrace_frame_get
functions.description: Fetches the current backtrace frame (frame pointer and program counter) for a thread. Used by the backtrace facility to start or sample a stack trace.
requirements: thread must be a valid rt_thread_t; may be the current thread
frame must be a non-NULL pointer to storage for the result
Caller should check the returned rt_err_t for success/failure (exact codes unknown)

functions.name: rt_hw_backtrace_frame_unwind
functions.description: Unwinds a backtrace frame for a thread, updating the frame to its caller (previous frame). Repeated calls step through the call stack.
requirements: thread must be a valid rt_thread_t; should match the thread used to obtain the initial frame
frame must be a non-NULL pointer and initially contain a valid frame (from rt_hw_backtrace_frame_get or prior unwind)
Caller should check the returned rt_err_t for success/failure (end-of-stack or errors)

functions.name: rt_hw_console_output
functions.description: Outputs a string to the low-level hardware console (e.g., UART). Intended for logging and early boot messages.
requirements: str must be a valid, null-terminated string pointer; may be large, but hardware FIFOs may limit throughput (exact limits unknown)
May be called from early boot or interrupt context depending on port capabilities (exact constraints unknown)

functions.name: rt_hw_show_memory
functions.description: Dumps a region of memory to the console for debugging, starting at addr for size bytes. Format is implementation-specific.
requirements: addr must reference a readable memory region mapped to the CPU
size should be non-zero to produce output; large ranges may take long time
Caller must ensure accessing the memory range is safe (no MMU/permission faults)

functions.name: rt_hw_exception_install
functions.description: Installs a global hardware exception handler callback that will be invoked when an exception occurs. The handler receives a context pointer and returns an rt_err_t.
requirements: exception_handle must be a valid function pointer; may not be NULL for enabling handling (NULL behavior unknown)
The handler must be safe to call in exception context (non-blocking, re-entrant as required by platform)

functions.name: rt_hw_us_delay
functions.description: Busy-waits for approximately the specified number of microseconds. Used for short hardware timing delays.
requirements: us is the delay in microseconds; must fit in rt_uint32_t
Should not be used for long delays as it may block the CPU and affect scheduling

functions.name: rt_hw_cpu_id
functions.description: Returns the current CPU/core ID on SMP systems, or 0 on uniprocessor ports. Useful for per-CPU operations.
requirements: Return value semantics are platform-defined; may be 0 on UP systems

functions.name: rt_hw_ipi_send
functions.signature: void rt_hw_ipi_send(int ipi_vector, unsigned int cpu_mask);
functions.description: Sends an inter-processor interrupt (IPI) identified by ipi_vector to CPUs selected by cpu_mask. Available when RT_USING_SMP or RT_USING_AMP is enabled.
requirements: Available only if RT_USING_SMP or RT_USING_AMP is defined
ipi_vector must be a valid IPI vector supported by the platform
cpu_mask selects target CPUs; bit layout is platform-specific and must reference existing CPUs

functions.name: rt_hw_spin_lock_init
functions.description: Initializes a hardware spinlock object. Available only on SMP builds where rt_hw_spinlock_t is defined.
requirements: Available only if RT_USING_SMP is defined
lock must be a non-NULL pointer to storage for a spinlock

functions.name: rt_hw_spin_lock
functions.description: Acquires a hardware spinlock, busy-waiting until it is obtained. On non-SMP builds this name is a macro that disables interrupts and stores the previous level in the provided variable.
requirements: In SMP builds (RT_USING_SMP defined) lock must be a valid initialized rt_hw_spinlock_t pointer
In non-SMP builds, this is a macro requiring 'lock' to be an lvalue rt_ubase_t variable; the macro assigns the disabled interrupt level into *lock
Caller must ensure balanced rt_hw_spin_unlock calls

functions.name: rt_hw_spin_unlock
functions.description: Releases a hardware spinlock. On non-SMP builds this name is a macro that restores interrupts using the level stored by rt_hw_spin_lock.
requirements: In SMP builds (RT_USING_SMP defined) lock must be a valid rt_hw_spinlock_t pointer previously locked
In non-SMP builds, this is a macro requiring 'lock' to be an lvalue rt_ubase_t variable previously set by rt_hw_spin_lock
Must be called exactly once for each successful rt_hw_spin_lock acquisition

functions.name: rt_hw_secondary_cpu_up
functions.description: Boots or releases the secondary CPUs in an SMP system. Typically called during SMP initialization.
requirements: Available only if RT_USING_SMP is defined
Must be called during system bring-up when it is safe to start secondary CPUs (exact sequencing unknown)

functions.name: rt_hw_secondary_cpu_idle_exec
functions.description: Idle loop body executed by secondary CPUs when there is no runnable task. Used internally by the SMP scheduler/idle thread.
requirements: Available only if RT_USING_SMP is defined
Intended to be called by the system idle context on secondary CPUs; not for general application use

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_load
functions.description: Loads and returns the current value of an atomic variable pointed to by ptr. Hardware-backed implementation (when available). Intended for concurrent/ISR-safe access to a shared atomic value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a properly initialized rt_atomic_t storage
ptr should reference memory suitable for concurrent access (shared/volatile)
Exact memory ordering semantics are unknown in this header (implementation-defined)

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_store
functions.description: Atomically stores val into the atomic variable at ptr. Hardware-backed implementation (when available).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
The stored value val must be representable in rt_atomic_t
Exact memory ordering semantics are unknown in this header (implementation-defined)

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_add
functions.description: Atomically adds val to *ptr and returns the previous value. Hardware-backed implementation (when available).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
The addition must not rely on undefined behavior (e.g., overflow handling is implementation-defined)
Exact memory ordering semantics are unknown in this header (implementation-defined)

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_sub
functions.description: Atomically subtracts val from *ptr and returns the previous value. Hardware-backed implementation (when available).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Subtraction overflow/underflow behavior is implementation-defined
Exact memory ordering semantics are unknown in this header (implementation-defined)

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_and
functions.description: Atomically performs bitwise AND of *ptr with val and returns the previous value. Hardware-backed implementation (when available).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Bitwise operation applies to integral rt_atomic_t
Exact memory ordering semantics are unknown in this header (implementation-defined)

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_or
functions.description: Atomically performs bitwise OR of *ptr with val and returns the previous value. Hardware-backed implementation (when available).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Bitwise operation applies to integral rt_atomic_t
Exact memory ordering semantics are unknown in this header (implementation-defined)

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_xor
functions.description: Atomically performs bitwise XOR of *ptr with val and returns the previous value. Hardware-backed implementation (when available).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Bitwise operation applies to integral rt_atomic_t
Exact memory ordering semantics are unknown in this header (implementation-defined)

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_exchange
functions.description: Atomically replaces *ptr with val and returns the previous value. Hardware-backed implementation (when available).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Exact memory ordering semantics are unknown in this header (implementation-defined)

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_flag_clear
functions.description: Atomically clears a flag at *ptr (typically sets to 0). Hardware-backed implementation (when available).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Caller should treat *ptr as a binary flag (0/1)

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_flag_test_and_set
functions.description: Atomically tests if flag at *ptr is set; if not set, sets it. Returns the previous flag value (0 if it was clear and now set, 1 if it was already set). Hardware-backed implementation (when available).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Caller should treat *ptr as a binary flag (0/1)

functions.name: rt_hw_atomic_compare_exchange_strong
functions.description: Atomically compares *ptr with *expected; if equal, writes desired to *ptr and returns 1. Otherwise, writes the current *ptr into *expected and returns 0. Hardware-backed implementation (when available).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
expected must be a valid, non-null pointer to rt_atomic_t for both input (expected value) and output (actual value on failure)
The function returns 1 on success, 0 on failure (as per naming and soft implementation)
Exact memory ordering semantics are unknown in this header (implementation-defined)

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_exchange
functions.signature: rt_inline rt_atomic_t rt_soft_atomic_exchange(volatile rt_atomic_t *ptr, rt_atomic_t val);
functions.description: Software fallback: atomically replaces *ptr with val by disabling interrupts around the critical section. Returns the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
May be called from normal and interrupt contexts; atomicity is provided by disabling interrupts
No assumptions about multi-core memory ordering are guaranteed by this software sequence

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_add
functions.signature: rt_inline rt_atomic_t rt_soft_atomic_add(volatile rt_atomic_t *ptr, rt_atomic_t val);
functions.description: Software fallback: atomically adds val to *ptr by disabling interrupts and returns the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Addition overflow/underflow behavior follows rt_atomic_t semantics (implementation-defined)
Callable in contexts where temporarily disabling interrupts is acceptable

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_sub
functions.signature: rt_inline rt_atomic_t rt_soft_atomic_sub(volatile rt_atomic_t *ptr, rt_atomic_t val);
functions.description: Software fallback: atomically subtracts val from *ptr by disabling interrupts and returns the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Callable in contexts where temporarily disabling interrupts is acceptable

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_xor
functions.signature: rt_inline rt_atomic_t rt_soft_atomic_xor(volatile rt_atomic_t *ptr, rt_atomic_t val);
functions.description: Software fallback: atomically applies bitwise XOR of *ptr with val by disabling interrupts and returns the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Callable in contexts where temporarily disabling interrupts is acceptable

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_and
functions.signature: rt_inline rt_atomic_t rt_soft_atomic_and(volatile rt_atomic_t *ptr, rt_atomic_t val);
functions.description: Software fallback: atomically applies bitwise AND of *ptr with val by disabling interrupts and returns the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Callable in contexts where temporarily disabling interrupts is acceptable

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_or
functions.signature: rt_inline rt_atomic_t rt_soft_atomic_or(volatile rt_atomic_t *ptr, rt_atomic_t val);
functions.description: Software fallback: atomically applies bitwise OR of *ptr with val by disabling interrupts and returns the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Callable in contexts where temporarily disabling interrupts is acceptable

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_load
functions.description: Software fallback: atomically loads and returns *ptr by briefly disabling interrupts.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a properly initialized rt_atomic_t
Callable in contexts where briefly disabling interrupts is acceptable

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_store
functions.signature: rt_inline void rt_soft_atomic_store(volatile rt_atomic_t *ptr, rt_atomic_t val);
functions.description: Software fallback: atomically stores val into *ptr by briefly disabling interrupts.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Callable in contexts where briefly disabling interrupts is acceptable

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_flag_test_and_set
functions.description: Software fallback: if *ptr is 0, sets it to 1 and returns 0; otherwise returns 1. Uses interrupt disable to ensure atomicity.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
The flag variable at *ptr is expected to be binary (0 or 1)

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_flag_clear
functions.description: Software fallback: clears a binary flag by setting *ptr to 0 atomically via interrupt disable.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
The flag variable at *ptr is expected to be binary (0 or 1)

functions.name: rt_soft_atomic_compare_exchange_strong
functions.signature: rt_inline rt_atomic_t rt_soft_atomic_compare_exchange_strong(volatile rt_atomic_t *ptr1, rt_atomic_t *ptr2, rt_atomic_t desired);
functions.description: Software fallback: compares *ptr1 with *ptr2; if equal, sets *ptr1 to desired and returns 1. Otherwise, writes *ptr1 into *ptr2 and returns 0. Implemented by disabling interrupts.
requirements: ptr1 must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
ptr2 must be a valid, non-null pointer to rt_atomic_t; on failure it is overwritten with the observed value
Returns 1 on success (exchange performed), 0 on failure (no exchange)
Callable in contexts where briefly disabling interrupts is acceptable

functions.name: rt_atomic_dec_and_test
functions.description: Atomically decrements *ptr by 1 and returns true if the new value is 0. Uses the selected rt_atomic_* backend.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Relies on rt_atomic_sub(ptr, 1) returning the previous value; evaluates equality to 1 to detect new value 0

functions.name: rt_atomic_fetch_add_unless
functions.signature: rt_inline rt_atomic_t rt_atomic_fetch_add_unless(volatile rt_atomic_t *ptr, rt_atomic_t a, rt_atomic_t u);
functions.description: Atomically adds a to *ptr unless *ptr equals u. Returns the value of *ptr observed before any addition. Retries using strong compare-exchange.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
The operation will not modify *ptr if its value equals u
On success when not equal to u, *ptr becomes previous_value + a
Caller should handle potential spinning if contention occurs

functions.name: rt_atomic_add_unless
functions.signature: rt_inline rt_bool_t rt_atomic_add_unless(volatile rt_atomic_t *ptr, rt_atomic_t a, rt_atomic_t u);
functions.description: Returns true if it added a to *ptr (i.e., *ptr was not equal to u); returns false if no addition occurred because *ptr equaled u.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Semantics depend on rt_atomic_fetch_add_unless; no addition occurs if *ptr equals u

functions.name: rt_atomic_inc_not_zero
functions.description: Atomically increments *ptr by 1 only if its value is not zero. Returns true if incremented, false if the value was zero.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
No increment occurs if *ptr equals 0

functions.name: rt_ll_slist_init
functions.description: Initializes a lock-less singly-linked list head by setting its next to 0. Intended as the initial setup for a LIFO single-list used with the accompanying atomic enqueue/dequeue functions.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-null pointer to an rt_ll_slist_t node representing the list head
Must be called before using l with rt_ll_slist_enqueue/rt_ll_slist_dequeue

functions.name: rt_ll_slist_enqueue
functions.description: Atomically pushes node n to the front of a lock-less singly-linked list headed by l (LIFO stack behavior), using a CAS loop on l->next.
requirements: l and n must be valid, non-null pointers to rt_ll_slist_t nodes
n->next will be overwritten; n must be prepared for insertion (not concurrently in another list)
l must have been initialized (e.g., via rt_ll_slist_init)
Safe for concurrent producers; ordering is LIFO

functions.name: rt_ll_slist_dequeue
functions.description: Atomically pops and returns the head node from a lock-less singly-linked list headed by l (LIFO). If the list is empty, returns NULL.
requirements: l must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized list head
Safe for concurrent access with rt_ll_slist_enqueue; returns NULL if empty

functions.name: rt_atomic_load
functions.description: Frontend macro mapping to the selected backend (C11 atomics, hardware atomics, or software fallback) to load the current value of an atomic variable at ptr.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a properly initialized rt_atomic_t
Actual memory ordering semantics depend on the chosen backend

functions.name: rt_atomic_store
functions.description: Frontend macro mapping to the selected backend to store v into the atomic variable at ptr.

v must be representable in rt_atomic_t

requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Overflow behavior is implementation-defined

functions.description: Frontend macro mapping to the selected backend to atomically subtract v from *ptr, returning the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Underflow behavior is implementation-defined
Actual memory ordering semantics depend on the chosen backend

functions.name: rt_atomic_and
functions.description: Frontend macro mapping to the selected backend to atomically bitwise-AND *ptr with v, returning the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Actual memory ordering semantics depend on the chosen backend

functions.name: rt_atomic_or
functions.description: Frontend macro mapping to the selected backend to atomically bitwise-OR *ptr with v, returning the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Actual memory ordering semantics depend on the chosen backend

functions.name: rt_atomic_xor
functions.description: Frontend macro mapping to the selected backend to atomically bitwise-XOR *ptr with v, returning the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Actual memory ordering semantics depend on the chosen backend

functions.name: rt_atomic_exchange
functions.description: Frontend macro mapping to the selected backend to atomically replace *ptr with v, returning the previous value.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Actual memory ordering semantics depend on the chosen backend

functions.name: rt_atomic_flag_clear
functions.description: Frontend macro mapping to the selected backend to atomically clear a binary flag at *ptr (set to 0).
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Treat *ptr as a binary flag (0/1)
Actual memory ordering semantics depend on the chosen backend

functions.name: rt_atomic_flag_test_and_set
functions.description: Frontend macro mapping to the selected backend to test-and-set a binary flag: returns previous value and sets to 1 if it was 0.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
Treat *ptr as a binary flag (0/1)
Actual memory ordering semantics depend on the chosen backend

functions.name: rt_atomic_compare_exchange_strong
functions.description: Frontend macro mapping to the selected backend to perform a strong compare-and-exchange: if *ptr equals *v, write des to *ptr and return 1; otherwise, write current *ptr to *v and return 0.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable rt_atomic_t
v must be a valid, non-null pointer to rt_atomic_t; used as in/out parameter for expected value
des must be representable in rt_atomic_t
Actual memory ordering semantics depend on the chosen backend

functions.name: entry
functions.description: Application or kernel entry point declared for GCC builds. Called by startup code to begin execution.
requirements: Must be linked as the program’s entry symbol by the BSP/build system.
Should return an int status code; 0 typically indicates success.

functions.name: rt_object_get_information
functions.description: Returns the global object information table for the specified RT-Thread object class.
requirements: type must be a valid enum rt_object_class_type.

functions.name: rt_object_get_length
functions.description: Returns the number of objects currently registered under the given object class.
requirements: type must be a valid enum rt_object_class_type.

functions.name: rt_object_get_pointers
functions.signature: int rt_object_get_pointers(enum rt_object_class_type type, rt_object_t *pointers, int maxlen);
functions.description: Retrieves up to maxlen pointers to objects of the specified class and stores them into pointers.
requirements: pointers must be a valid, writable array with capacity of at least maxlen entries.
maxlen must be non-negative.
type must be a valid enum rt_object_class_type.

functions.name: rt_object_init
functions.signature: void rt_object_init(struct rt_object *object, enum rt_object_class_type type, const char *name);

functions.name: rt_object_detach

Object must not be in use by other subsystems at the time of detachment (unknown exact rules).

functions.name: rt_object_allocate
functions.signature: rt_object_t rt_object_allocate(enum rt_object_class_type type, const char *name);

type must be a valid enum rt_object_class_type.
name should be a valid null-terminated string.
Caller must later call rt_object_delete to free the object.

functions.name: rt_object_delete
functions.description: Deletes a heap-allocated kernel object and frees associated resources.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
object must be a valid object previously created by rt_object_allocate or corresponding create API.
Object must not be in active use when deleted (unknown exact rules).

functions.name: rt_custom_object_create
functions.description: Creates a custom kernel object with user-provided data and a data destructor callback.
