name must be a valid string.
data may be any pointer stored with the object.
data_destroy, if non-NULL, must be callable at destroy time and handle provided data.

functions.name: rt_custom_object_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a custom kernel object created with rt_custom_object_create, invoking the registered data destructor if provided.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
obj must be a valid custom object.
Must not be in active use at destroy time (unknown exact rules).

functions.name: rt_object_is_systemobject
functions.description: Returns whether the object is a system (statically allocated) object rather than a heap object.
requirements: object must be a valid rt_object_t.

functions.name: rt_object_get_type
functions.description: Gets the object’s type as an 8-bit code representing its object class.
requirements: object must be a valid rt_object_t.

functions.name: rt_object_for_each
functions.signature: rt_err_t rt_object_for_each(rt_uint8_t type, rt_object_iter_t iter, void *data);
functions.description: Iterates over all objects of the given type, invoking the iterator callback for each.
requirements: type is an object class identifier.
iter must be a valid function pointer of type rt_object_iter_t; it must not block indefinitely or corrupt iteration.
data is user context passed to callback.

functions.name: rt_object_find
functions.description: Finds an object by name and type and returns its handle, or RT_NULL if not found.
requirements: name must be a valid null-terminated string.
type is an object class identifier.

functions.name: rt_object_get_name
functions.signature: rt_err_t rt_object_get_name(rt_object_t object, char *name, rt_uint8_t name_size);
functions.description: Copies the object’s name into the provided buffer.
requirements: object must be valid.
name must be a writable buffer with size at least name_size.
name_size must be greater than 0.

functions.name: rt_object_attach_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook called when an object is attached/registered in the object system.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL to clear; if non-NULL it must return quickly and not block.

functions.name: rt_object_detach_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook called when an object is detached/unregistered.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL to clear; if non-NULL it must not block.

functions.name: rt_object_trytake_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook called when an object is attempted to be taken/locked (try operation).
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; hooks must be lightweight and non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_object_take_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook called after an object is taken/locked.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; hooks must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_object_put_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook called when an object is released/unlocked.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; hooks must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_tick_get
functions.description: Returns the current system tick count.

functions.name: rt_tick_get_delta
functions.description: Returns the tick delta between current tick and the provided base tick, handling wraparound as per implementation.
requirements: base is a previously captured tick value.

functions.name: rt_tick_set
functions.description: Sets the current system tick counter to the specified value.
requirements: Must be called in a privileged/system context per BSP policy (unknown exact rules).

functions.name: rt_tick_increase
functions.description: Increments the system tick by one; typically called from the system tick ISR.
requirements: Should be called by the system timer interrupt handler.

functions.name: rt_tick_increase_tick
functions.description: Increments the system tick by a specified amount.
requirements: tick is the number of ticks to add; should be positive or zero.

functions.name: rt_tick_from_millisecond
functions.description: Converts milliseconds to system ticks based on the configured tick rate.
requirements: ms may be negative or positive; behavior on negative values depends on implementation (unknown).

functions.name: rt_tick_get_millisecond
functions.description: Returns the elapsed time in milliseconds derived from the system tick count.

functions.name: rt_tick_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook function invoked on each system tick.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL to clear; if non-NULL, it must be short and non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_system_timer_init
functions.description: Initializes the kernel timer subsystem. Must be called during system init before timers are used.
requirements: Call once at startup before creating or starting timers.

functions.name: rt_system_timer_thread_init
functions.description: Creates/initializes the system timer service thread that processes timer events.
requirements: Must be called after scheduler prerequisites are set but before timers are started (exact order implementation-specific).

functions.name: rt_timer_init
functions.signature: void rt_timer_init(rt_timer_t timer, const char *name, void (*timeout)(void *parameter), void *parameter, rt_tick_t time, rt_uint8_t flag);
functions.description: Initializes a statically allocated software timer with a callback, timeout, and behavior flags.
requirements: timer must be a valid, writable timer object.
name must be a valid string.
timeout must be a valid function pointer; must not block for long.
time specifies initial timeout in ticks; must be >= 0 (unsigned).
flag must be a valid timer option combination as defined by RT-Thread.

functions.name: rt_timer_detach
functions.description: Detaches a statically allocated timer from the system timer list without freeing memory.
requirements: timer must be a valid initialized timer.
Timer should be stopped before detaching (unknown if enforced).

functions.name: rt_timer_create
functions.signature: rt_timer_t rt_timer_create(const char *name, void (*timeout)(void *parameter), void *parameter, rt_tick_t time, rt_uint8_t flag);
functions.description: Creates a heap-based software timer and returns its handle.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
name must be a valid string.
timeout must be a callable function pointer.
Caller must delete with rt_timer_delete when done.

functions.name: rt_timer_delete
functions.description: Deletes a heap-allocated timer and frees associated resources.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
timer must be created by rt_timer_create.
Timer should be stopped or not in use (unknown if enforced).

functions.name: rt_timer_start
functions.description: Starts or arms the specified timer for its configured timeout.
requirements: timer must be a valid initialized or created timer.

functions.name: rt_timer_stop
functions.description: Stops the specified timer if running.
requirements: timer must be valid.

functions.name: rt_timer_control
functions.signature: rt_err_t rt_timer_control(rt_timer_t timer, int cmd, void *arg);
functions.description: Controls timer parameters at runtime via command codes (e.g., set period, one-shot/periodic).
requirements: timer must be valid.
cmd must be a recognized control command; arg type/meaning depends on cmd.

functions.name: rt_timer_next_timeout_tick
functions.description: Returns the next soonest timer expiration tick value, or a sentinel if none.

functions.name: rt_timer_check
functions.description: Scans and processes expired timers; typically called by the timer thread or tick handler.
requirements: Should be invoked by system internals; callers must ensure proper context (non-interrupt unless designed) (unknown).

functions.name: rt_timer_enter_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook invoked when a timer callback is about to be entered.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook must be lightweight and non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_timer_exit_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook invoked when a timer callback has finished executing.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook must be lightweight and non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_thread_init
functions.signature: rt_err_t rt_thread_init(struct rt_thread *thread, const char *name, void (*entry)(void *parameter), void *parameter, void *stack_start, rt_uint32_t stack_size, rt_uint8_t priority, rt_uint32_t tick);
functions.description: Initializes a statically allocated thread with entry function, stack, priority, and time slice.
requirements: thread must be a valid, writable struct rt_thread.
name must be a valid string.
entry must be a valid function pointer; it should not return or must handle return appropriately.
stack_start must point to a buffer of at least stack_size bytes aligned per port requirements.
priority must be within supported range (implementation-defined).
tick is the time slice in ticks.

functions.name: rt_thread_detach
functions.description: Detaches a statically allocated thread object from scheduler management without freeing memory.
requirements: thread must be a valid initialized thread.
Thread should not be running or must be stopped before detaching (unknown if enforced).

functions.name: rt_thread_create
functions.signature: rt_thread_t rt_thread_create(const char *name, void (*entry)(void *parameter), void *parameter, rt_uint32_t stack_size, rt_uint8_t priority, rt_uint32_t tick);
functions.description: Creates a heap-allocated thread and returns its handle.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
name must be a valid string.
entry must be a valid function pointer.
stack_size must meet minimum/maximum constraints (implementation-defined).
priority within supported range.
Caller must delete with rt_thread_delete or close appropriately.

functions.name: rt_thread_delete
functions.description: Deletes a heap-allocated thread and frees resources.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
thread must be created by rt_thread_create.
Thread should not be running or must be properly stopped/terminated before deletion (unknown specifics).

functions.name: rt_thread_close
functions.description: Closes a thread object, releasing resources without freeing memory for statically allocated threads.
requirements: thread must be a valid thread object.
Thread should no longer be scheduled or running (unknown specifics).

functions.name: rt_thread_self
functions.description: Returns the current running thread’s handle, or RT_NULL if called before scheduler start or in special contexts.

functions.name: rt_thread_find
functions.description: Finds a thread by name and returns its handle, or RT_NULL if not found.
requirements: name must be a valid null-terminated string.

functions.name: rt_thread_startup
functions.description: Transitions a newly created/initialized thread to the ready state so it can be scheduled.
requirements: thread must be a valid thread initialized/created and not already started.

functions.name: rt_thread_yield
functions.description: Yields the processor voluntarily, allowing the scheduler to run another ready thread.
requirements: Must be called in thread context.

functions.name: rt_thread_delay
functions.description: Puts the current thread to sleep for the specified number of ticks.
requirements: Must be called in thread context.
tick is a delay duration in ticks.

functions.name: rt_thread_delay_until
functions.description: Delays the current thread until the absolute tick specified by *tick + inc_tick, updating *tick for periodic waits.
requirements: Must be called in thread context.
tick must be a valid pointer to a stored absolute tick.
inc_tick is the interval in ticks.

functions.name: rt_thread_mdelay
functions.description: Delays the current thread for the specified number of milliseconds.
requirements: Must be called in thread context.
ms must be non-negative (behavior for negative unknown).

functions.name: rt_thread_control
functions.signature: rt_err_t rt_thread_control(rt_thread_t thread, int cmd, void *arg);
functions.description: Controls or queries a thread via command codes (e.g., priority change, affinity).
requirements: thread must be valid (some cmds may allow RT_NULL for current).
cmd must be recognized by implementation; arg semantics depend on cmd.

functions.name: rt_thread_suspend
functions.description: Suspends the specified thread, removing it from scheduling until resumed.
requirements: thread must be valid.
Must not be called on the current thread in contexts where suspension is illegal (e.g., interrupt).

functions.name: rt_thread_suspend_with_flag
functions.description: Suspends a thread with additional suspend flags influencing behavior.
requirements: thread must be valid.
suspend_flag must be a valid combination defined by RT-Thread.

functions.name: rt_thread_resume
functions.description: Resumes a suspended thread, making it schedulable.
requirements: thread must be valid and currently suspended.

functions.name: rt_thread_wakeup
functions.description: Wakes a thread using the wakeup framework in SMART builds.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SMART to be enabled.
thread must be valid.

functions.name: rt_thread_wakeup_set
functions.signature: void rt_thread_wakeup_set(struct rt_thread *thread, rt_wakeup_func_t func, void* user_data);
functions.description: Sets a custom wakeup handler and user data for a thread in SMART builds.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SMART to be enabled.
thread must be valid.
func may be NULL to clear; if non-NULL must be callable in appropriate context.

functions.name: rt_thread_get_name
functions.signature: rt_err_t rt_thread_get_name(rt_thread_t thread, char *name, rt_uint8_t name_size);
functions.description: Copies the thread’s name into the provided buffer.
requirements: thread must be valid.
name must be a writable buffer of at least name_size.
name_size must be > 0.

functions.name: rt_thread_get_usage
functions.description: Returns CPU usage percentage (0-100) for the specified thread.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_CPU_USAGE_TRACER to be enabled.
thread must be valid.

functions.name: rt_thread_alloc_sig
functions.description: Allocates signal handling structures for the specified thread.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SIGNALS to be enabled.
tid must be valid.

functions.name: rt_thread_free_sig
functions.description: Releases/free signal handling resources for the specified thread.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SIGNALS to be enabled.
tid must be valid.

functions.name: rt_thread_kill
functions.description: Sends a signal to the specified thread.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SIGNALS to be enabled.
tid must be valid.
sig must be a valid signal number supported by the system.

functions.name: rt_thread_suspend_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook called when a thread is suspended.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; hook must be quick and non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_thread_resume_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook called when a thread is resumed.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; hook must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_thread_idle_init
functions.description: Initializes the idle thread for the system.
requirements: Call during system initialization before scheduler start.

functions.name: rt_thread_idle_sethook
functions.description: Adds a hook to be executed in the idle thread loop.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK or RT_USING_IDLE_HOOK to be enabled.
hook must be quick and must never block or suspend.
Returns -RT_EFULL if the hook list is full.

functions.name: rt_thread_idle_delhook
functions.description: Removes a previously registered idle hook.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK or RT_USING_IDLE_HOOK to be enabled.
hook must match a previously added hook.

functions.name: rt_thread_idle_gethandler
functions.description: Returns the idle thread handle.

functions.name: rt_system_scheduler_init
functions.description: Initializes the system scheduler structures.
requirements: Call once during system initialization before creating/starting threads.

functions.name: rt_system_scheduler_start
functions.description: Starts the scheduler, enabling task switching.
requirements: Must be called after scheduler and initial threads are initialized.
Typically does not return.

functions.name: rt_schedule
functions.description: Triggers a scheduling decision to switch to the highest-priority ready thread.
requirements: Generally called in thread or ISR-tail context as allowed by port (unknown).

functions.name: rt_scheduler_do_irq_switch
functions.description: Performs a context switch requested during interrupt processing using the provided context.
requirements: context must point to an architecture-defined context structure.

functions.name: rt_scheduler_stack_check
functions.description: Performs a stack overflow/usage check for the specified thread when overflow checking is enabled.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_OVERFLOW_CHECK to be enabled.
thread must be valid.

functions.name: rt_enter_critical
functions.description: Enters a critical section, disabling scheduling/interrupts as implemented, and returns the previous state/level.
requirements: Caller must later call rt_exit_critical or rt_exit_critical_safe with the returned level to restore.

functions.name: rt_exit_critical
functions.description: Leaves a critical section entered by rt_enter_critical, restoring previous state.
requirements: Must be paired with a previous rt_enter_critical on the same context.

functions.name: rt_exit_critical_safe
functions.description: Restores the critical section state to the provided level, safely exiting nested critical sections.
requirements: critical_level must be a value previously returned by rt_enter_critical for this context.

functions.name: rt_critical_level
functions.description: Returns the current critical section nesting level or scheduler lock depth.

functions.name: rt_scheduler_stack_overflow_sethook
functions.description: Sets a hook invoked when a stack overflow is detected for a thread; hook may return an error code.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL to clear; must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_scheduler_sethook
functions.description: Registers a scheduler hook called when switching from one thread to another.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; must be non-blocking and quick.

functions.name: rt_scheduler_switch_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook called on thread switch events with the target thread.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_secondary_cpu_entry
functions.description: Entry point for secondary CPUs in SMP systems to start RT-Thread scheduling on that core.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SMP to be enabled.
Called by platform-specific bring-up code.

functions.name: rt_scheduler_ipi_handler
functions.description: Handles inter-processor interrupt (IPI) for scheduler coordination in SMP systems.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SMP to be enabled.
vector is the interrupt vector number; param is platform-defined.

functions.name: rt_signal_mask
functions.description: Masks (blocks) delivery of the specified signal number to the current thread or context.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SIGNALS to be enabled.
signo must be a valid signal number.

functions.name: rt_signal_unmask
functions.description: Unmasks (unblocks) the specified signal number.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SIGNALS to be enabled.
signo must be a valid signal number.

functions.name: rt_signal_check
functions.description: Checks for pending signals and possibly alters the provided context; returns an updated or original context pointer.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SIGNALS to be enabled.
context must be a valid architecture-defined context pointer or NULL per implementation.

functions.name: rt_signal_install
functions.description: Installs a signal handler for the specified signal; returns previous handler.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SIGNALS to be enabled.
signo must be valid; handler must be a valid function pointer or SIG_IGN/SIG_DFL equivalent.

functions.name: rt_signal_wait
functions.signature: int rt_signal_wait(const rt_sigset_t *set, rt_siginfo_t *si, rt_int32_t timeout);
functions.description: Waits for any signal in the set with optional timeout, returning the signal number or an error code.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SIGNALS to be enabled.
set must be a valid pointer to a signal set.
si may be NULL or must point to writable info storage if non-NULL.
timeout in ticks; negative may indicate infinite wait depending on implementation (unknown).

functions.name: rt_system_signal_init
functions.description: Initializes the signal subsystem.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SIGNALS to be enabled.
Call during system initialization before using signals.

functions.name: rt_mp_init
functions.signature: rt_err_t rt_mp_init(struct rt_mempool *mp, const char *name, void *start, rt_size_t size, rt_size_t block_size);
functions.description: Initializes a fixed-block memory pool over a given memory region.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_MEMPOOL to be enabled.
mp must be a valid writable mempool structure.
name must be a valid string.
start must point to a memory region of at least size bytes.
block_size must be > 0 and fit within size.

functions.name: rt_mp_detach
functions.description: Detaches a statically initialized memory pool from the system without freeing the backing memory.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_MEMPOOL to be enabled.
mp must be a valid initialized mempool.

functions.name: rt_mp_create
functions.signature: rt_mp_t rt_mp_create(const char *name, rt_size_t block_count, rt_size_t block_size);
functions.description: Creates a heap-based memory pool with block_count blocks of block_size each.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_MEMPOOL and RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
name must be a valid string.
block_count and block_size must be > 0.
Caller must delete with rt_mp_delete.

functions.name: rt_mp_delete
functions.description: Deletes a heap-allocated memory pool and frees its memory.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_MEMPOOL and RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
mp must be a valid pool created by rt_mp_create.
All allocated blocks should be freed before deletion (unknown enforcement).

functions.name: rt_mp_alloc
functions.description: Allocates a block from the memory pool, optionally waiting up to time ticks.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_MEMPOOL to be enabled.
mp must be valid.
time may be RT_WAITING_FOREVER or a non-negative timeout per RT-Thread conventions (exact constants unknown).

functions.name: rt_mp_free
functions.description: Frees a block previously allocated from a memory pool.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_MEMPOOL to be enabled.
block must be a pointer returned by rt_mp_alloc from a live pool.

functions.name: rt_mp_alloc_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook called on memory pool block allocation.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_MEMPOOL and RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_mp_free_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook called on memory pool block free.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_MEMPOOL and RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_system_heap_init
functions.description: Initializes the system heap with the memory region [begin_addr, end_addr).
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
begin_addr and end_addr must define a valid non-empty memory range; begin_addr < end_addr.
Call once during system initialization before heap allocations.

functions.name: rt_system_heap_init_generic
functions.description: Initializes a generic heap backend over the provided memory region.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
begin_addr and end_addr must define a valid range.
Call during system initialization.

functions.name: rt_malloc
functions.description: Allocates size bytes from the system heap.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
size may be zero (behavior implementation-defined).

functions.name: rt_free
functions.description: Frees a heap block previously allocated by rt_malloc/rt_realloc/rt_calloc.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
ptr must be a pointer returned by RT-Thread heap APIs; NULL is allowed (no-op) per typical conventions (unknown if strict).

functions.name: rt_realloc
functions.description: Resizes a previously allocated heap block to newsize bytes, possibly moving it.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
ptr may be NULL to behave like malloc; newsize may be 0 to free (behavior implementation-defined).

functions.name: rt_calloc
functions.description: Allocates an array of count elements of size bytes each, zero-initialized.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
count and size must be such that count*size does not overflow.

functions.name: rt_malloc_align
functions.description: Allocates size bytes from the heap with the specified power-of-two alignment.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
align should be a power of two and >= architecture minimum alignment.

functions.name: rt_free_align
functions.description: Frees a block allocated by rt_malloc_align.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
ptr must be a pointer returned by rt_malloc_align.

functions.name: rt_memory_info
functions.description: Retrieves heap statistics: total, currently used, and maximum used sizes.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HEAP to be enabled.
total, used, and max_used must be valid writable pointers.

functions.name: rt_page_alloc
functions.description: Allocates npages pages from the SLAB page allocator when used as heap.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SLAB and RT_USING_SLAB_AS_HEAP to be enabled.
npages must be > 0.

functions.name: rt_page_free
functions.description: Frees npages pages previously allocated by rt_page_alloc.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SLAB and RT_USING_SLAB_AS_HEAP to be enabled.
addr must be page-aligned and returned by rt_page_alloc.
npages must match the allocation size (unknown if flexible).

functions.name: rt_malloc_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook invoked on malloc operations with pointer out-parameter and size.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_realloc_set_entry_hook
functions.description: Registers a hook invoked before realloc with existing pointer and requested size.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_realloc_set_exit_hook
functions.description: Registers a hook invoked after realloc with updated pointer and size.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_free_sethook
functions.description: Registers a hook invoked on free operations with pointer out-parameter.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_HOOK to be enabled.
hook may be NULL; must be non-blocking.

functions.name: rt_smem_init
functions.signature: rt_smem_t rt_smem_init(const char *name, void *begin_addr, rt_size_t size);
functions.description: Initializes a small memory allocator over a given region and returns its handle.
requirements: Requires RT_USING_SMALL_MEM to be enabled.
name must be a valid string.
begin_addr must point to a region of at least size bytes.

functions.name: rt_smem_detach

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets ASCII/UTF-8 strings used by many stubs as names and identifiers.
# The fuzzer harness will consume the returned bytes as the initial corpus buffer
# for FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME etc. We therefore craft name-like strings
# with varied lengths, character classes, and common RT-Thread name patterns to
# exercise lookups and create/init APIs that clamp names to <=31 bytes.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(0, len(seq))]

def _make_name(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # RT-Thread often limits names to 31 chars. Produce diverse names:
    # - short/empty
    # - exact boundary 31
    # - mixed symbols, digits, underscores
    # - common prefixes for objects: th_, sem_, mut_, evt_, mb_, mq_
    prefixes = ["", "th_", "sem_", "mut_", "evt_", "mb_", "mq_", "dev_", "cpu_", "t_", "obj_"]
    base_sets = [
        string.ascii_lowercase,
        string.ascii_uppercase,
        string.digits,
        string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_",
        string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_",
    ]
    # choose target length with bias to interesting edges
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 30, 31, max(1, max_len - 1), max_len]
    # clamp to max_len
    target_len = min(max_len, _rand_choice(rng, choices))
    prefix = _rand_choice(rng, prefixes)
    remaining = max(0, target_len - len(prefix))
    charset = _rand_choice(rng, base_sets)
    s = prefix + ''.join(rng.choice(charset) for _ in range(remaining))
    return s

def _make_utf8_edge(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Include some multibyte UTF-8 to test non-ASCII paths while remaining valid
    # Use a small palette of safe codepoints
    utf_blocks = [
        "线程",  # Chinese for thread
        "信号",  # signal
        "设备",  # device
        "队列",  # queue
        "事件",  # event
        "ΔΘ",    # Greek
        "✓✗",    # check marks
        "µs",     # microseconds
    ]
    base = _make_name(rng, max(0, max_len - 2))
    extra = _rand_choice(rng, utf_blocks)
    s = (base + extra)[:max_len]
    return s

def _compose_multi_names(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose several newline-separated names to seed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads
    parts = []
    # Produce a mix of ASCII and UTF-8 names with different target maxima seen in stubs (<=31, <=64, <=128)
    for max_len in (31, 31, 64, 128, 31, 64):
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append(_make_utf8_edge(rng, max_len))
        else:
            parts.append(_make_name(rng, max_len))
    blob = "\n".join(parts)
    return blob.encode('utf-8')

def _append_numeric_hints(rng: random.Random, buf: bytearray) -> None:
    # Many stubs also consume unsigned ints for flags/sizes; include textual numerics that
    # corpus-based engines may repurpose or the harness may place in the random source.
    interesting = [
        0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256,
        512, 1024, 1409, 1536, 4096,
        0x80, 0xFF, 0x100, 0x12,
    ]
    rng.shuffle(interesting)
    nums = ",".join(str(x) for x in interesting[:rng.randint(8, 16)])
    tag = f"\n#nums:{nums}\n"
    buf.extend(tag.encode('ascii'))

def _append_sections(rng: random.Random, buf: bytearray) -> None:
    # Add labeled sections that look like object declarations to bias dictionary extraction
    sections = []
    for kind in ("thread", "sem", "mutex", "event", "mb", "mq", "device"):
        nm = _make_name(rng, 31)
        sections.append(f"{kind}:{nm}")
    payload = "\n".join(sections) + "\n"
    buf.extend(payload.encode('utf-8'))

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Start with multiple candidate names
    out = bytearray()
    out.extend(_compose_multi_names(rng))
    # Add a few long lines to exercise longer truncations
    for _ in range(2):
        long_name = _make_name(rng, 256)
        out.extend(b"\n")
        out.extend(long_name.encode('utf-8'))
    # Add UTF-8 edge strings
    for _ in range(2):
        out.extend(b"\n")
        out.extend(_make_utf8_edge(rng, 64).encode('utf-8'))
    # Numeric and section hints
    _append_numeric_hints(rng, out)
    _append_sections(rng, out)
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(out) > MAX_BYTES:
        return bytes(out[:MAX_BYTES])
    return bytes(out)

import os
import random
import struct

# This generator crafts arbitrary binary data tailored to the target stubs:
# - rt_hw_cpu_{i,d}cache_ops use FUZZ_PARAM_STR as an addressable buffer. Any non-empty bytes are valid.
# - rt_mp_{init,detach} construct a mempool over a local buffer; no specific content required but variety helps.
# - rt_mq_send* stubs need payload of exactly msg_sz bytes, but msg_sz is provided via container attr in the fuzzer.
#   We therefore supply diverse payload sizes and contents so the fuzzer can resize/truncate/extend as needed.
# Strategy: produce a small header that includes multiple self-delimiting segments the harness will draw from
# via FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. Include varied sizes, alignments, and byte patterns.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of patterns: repeated fills, gradients, printable text, and fully random
    choice = rng.randrange(6)
    if choice == 0:
        # Repeating single byte
        b = rng.randrange(256)
        return bytes([b]) * n
    elif choice == 1:
        # Alternating pattern
        a, b = rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256)
        return bytes((a if (i & 1) == 0 else b) for i in range(n))
    elif choice == 2:
        # Incrementing ramp
        start = rng.randrange(256)
        return bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF) for i in range(n))
    elif choice == 3:
        # ASCII text with newlines and zeros sprinkled
        alphabet = (b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. \n\t\0" )
        return bytes(alphabet[rng.randrange(len(alphabet))] for _ in range(n))
    elif choice == 4:
        # Word-aligned pattern
        w = rng.getrandbits(32)
        chunk = struct.pack('<I', w)
        return (chunk * (n // 4) + chunk[: n % 4])
    else:
        # Fully random
        return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _make_segment(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    ln = rng.randrange(min_len, max_len + 1)
    return _rand_bytes(rng, ln)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build several segments to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers in a run.
    # Include variety in sizes to cover small and larger buffers.
    segments = []

    # Segment A: small buffer for cache ops (1..128 bytes)
    segments.append(_make_segment(rng, 1, 128))

    # Segment B: medium buffer (64..512)
    segments.append(_make_segment(rng, 64, 512))

    # Segment C: larger pool-like buffer (256..1536) suitable for mempool backing
    segments.append(_make_segment(rng, 256, 1536))

    # Segment D: message payload sized around typical MQ sizes (8..128)
    segments.append(_make_segment(rng, 8, 128))

    # Segment E: exact powers of two length to test alignment-sensitive paths (32, 64, 128, 256)
    pow2_len = rng.choice([32, 64, 128, 256])
    segments.append(_rand_bytes(rng, pow2_len))

    # Segment F: include zeros to test boundary cases
    zero_len = rng.randrange(16, 128)
    segments.append(b"\x00" * zero_len)

    # Segment G: include high-entropy random chunk (random 100..400)
    segments.append(_make_segment(rng, 100, 400))

    # Prepend a simple directory to allow the harness to split if needed: count + lengths
    # Format: b"FZ\x01" magic, u8 count, then for each: u16 length, then data
    header = bytearray()
    header += b"FZ\x01"
    count = len(segments)
    header.append(count & 0xFF)

    body = bytearray()
    for seg in segments:
        ln = len(seg)
        header += struct.pack('<H', ln)
        body += seg

    out = bytes(header) + bytes(body)
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return out
